title: Gradualist slew autoscaler with cost-feedback and kernel-awareness
creator: Avery Chen
description: Background: Dedicated fleets occasionally exhibit oscillatory capacity changes during short traffic spikes which increases cost and hurts tail latency. Current autoscalers either react quickly (causing cost and instability) or are conservative (missing short-lived throughput needs). Goal: implement a 'gradualist slew' autoscaler that blends multi-horizon target metrics, explicit slew-rate enforcement, and a closed-loop cost-feedback term. Additionally, make the controller kernel-aware: scaling step size and prioritization should consider recent GPU kernel occupancy and model KV-cache pressure so we avoid adding capacity that cannot be efficiently utilized.
solution_outline: 1) Metrics: synthesize a composite target from throughput (tokens/s and requests/s), latency percentiles (p50/p95), and queue depth. 2) Algorithm: proportional-derivative controller augmented with exponential moving average demand forecast + slew-rate limiter (max % change per minute). 3) Cost-feedback: penalize scaling that increases expected token unit cost beyond a configurable budget by reducing aggressive upscaling. 4) Kernel awareness: fetch recent GPU occupancy and avg kernel-duration; prefer vertical scaling (add GPU-backed slots) where kernel-utilization < threshold; otherwise prefer conservative steps. 5) Safety fences: per-tenant headroom min/max, global emergency cap, and rapid fall-back policy to a warm spare pool when latency breaches critical SLOs.
acceptance_criteria: Simulator shows >=30% reduction in scaling churn metric (scale events per hour) compared to current heuristic autoscaler for synthetic spike workloads
For customer A (high-throughput embedder) p95 latency not increased by more than 5% during controlled surge tests while cost delta <= +8%
Autoscaler enforces configurable slew limit (default 20% capacity change per 5 minutes) and honors per-tenant headroom settings
Kernel-awareness heuristic prevents >2 consecutive ineffective scale-ups (where added capacity usage < 20% after 3 minutes) in stagged kernel scenarios
Feature gated rollout available in console with telemetry for decisions, predicted vs actual demand, and cost delta estimates
implementation_notes: Data inputs: incoming time-series for tokens/s, rps, queue depth, latency p50/p95, GPU occupancy, kernel-duration histogram, and current committed capacity. Controller internals: compute short/medium/long EMA forecasts (T=30s, 3m, 10m). Produce candidate_scale = base_pd_control + forecast_adjustment. Apply cost_penalty = clamp(1 - alpha * (est_unit_cost - cost_budget)/cost_budget, 0.5, 1.0) before finalizing. Apply slew limiter and safety fences. Metrics exported via telemetry path: scaling_decision_{reason}, predicted_capacity, final_capacity, cost_estimate. Add an offline simulator harness (python) that replays historical production traces and models GPU occupancy to tune alpha and slew defaults.
progress_updates: 2025-10-08 - Ticket created with initial proposal and scope. Asked for PM and infra review.
2025-10-10 - Prototype PD controller implemented in sandbox; initial sims show reduced oscillation but slower recovery on 5s spikes.

2025-10-12 - Kernel-awareness hook integrated: GPU occupancy read added to telemetry stream (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/telemetry/pull/421). Sim results: prevented two wasted scale-ups on model X traces.

2025-10-14 - Design review with PM and SRE. Agreed to default slew-rate 20%/5m and conservative alpha=0.6 cost penalty. Decided to surface decision rationale in console rollout UI. Assigned QA scenario set.
2025-10-15 - End-to-end integration test scheduled on staging for 2025-10-22. Created simulator job and initial results uploaded to dashboard (https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/scale-sim/gradualist-v1).
review_feedback: PM (Morgan Brooks): please include a 'budget override' knob for enterprise customers with committed spend; ensure fail-open behavior documented
SRE (Leah Martinez): prefer hard global emergency cap rather than only soft fences; asked for post-mortem playbook if fallback pool saturates
Runtime Eng (Diego Ruiz): kernel-awareness is promising but add a smoothing window for occupancy to avoid noisy telemetry driving oscillation
Security (Priya Sharma): no sensitive data usage in telemetry; confirm GPU telemetry sanitized before export
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: slower reaction may violate tail SLOs on very short spikes -> Mitigation: emergency warm-spare pool and fall-back to 'rapid mode' when p99 > emergency_threshold
Risk: noisy GPU occupancy could cause flip-flops -> Mitigation: 30s smoothing window and require occupancy delta >10% for kernel-driven step changes
Risk: cost-feedback over-correction throttles legitimate scale-ups -> Mitigation: limit cost_penalty lower bound to 0.5 and log decision rationale for troubleshooting
qa_plan: Add unit tests for PD control math and cost_penalty behavior
Run simulator against 30 historical production traces and compare churn/latency/cost metrics
Staging chaos test: synthetic traffic spikes (5s, 30s, 3m) across 3 model types with and without kernel contention
Canary rollout to 10% of dedicated fleets with monitoring alerts and automatic rollback on threshold breaches
follow_ups: Post-canary tuning: refine alpha and slew defaults based on fleet telemetry
Consolidate console UX knobs and add enterprise override per PM feedback
Document playbook for emergency fallback and outages in Runbook repo
